hints: At constant speed on horizontal ground, driving force equals resistance: $F_D = 1150\text{ N}$.
Use the power formula $P = F_D \times v$ with $v = 12\text{ m s}^{-1}$.
Multiply $1150 \times 12$ to obtain the power output in watts.
walkthrough:
State the relation between power, driving force, and speed:
$$P = F_D \times v$$

Because the tractor travels at constant velocity on a horizontal surface, acceleration is zero ($a = 0$), so the driving force exactly matches the resistance force:
$$F_D = F_{\text{res}} = 1150\text{ N}$$

Substitute $F_D = 1150\text{ N}$ and velocity $v = 12\text{ m s}^{-1}$:
$$P = 1150 \times 12 = 13800\text{ W}$$

hints: Calculate the driving force at the base of the hill when power is $25\text{ kW} = 25000\text{ W}$ and speed is still $12\text{ m s}^{-1}$: $F_D = \frac{25000}{12}\text{ N}$.
Identify the opposing forces acting down the $4^\circ$ slope: resistance $1150\text{ N}$ and the downslope component of weight $mg\sin 4^\circ = 3700(10)\sin 4^\circ = 37000\sin 4^\circ$.
Apply Newton's second law along the slope: $F_D - 1150 - 37000\sin 4^\circ = 3700a$.
Solve for $a$, and state deceleration as the positive magnitude: $0.445\text{ m s}^{-2}$.
walkthrough:
Determine the driving force $F_D$ at the instant climbing commences, when $P = 25000\text{ W}$ and speed is $v = 12\text{ m s}^{-1}$:
$$F_D = \frac{P}{v} = \frac{25000}{12}\text{ N}$$

State Newton's second law along the slope directed upwards:
$$F_{\text{net}} = ma \implies F_D - F_{\text{res}} - mg\sin\theta = ma$$

Substitute the parameters $m = 3700\text{ kg}$, $g = 10\text{ m s}^{-2}$, $\theta = 4^\circ$, and $F_{\text{res}} = 1150\text{ N}$:
$$\frac{25000}{12} - 1150 - 3700(10)\sin 4^\circ = 3700a$$

Because the acceleration is negative, the tractor is decelerating. The deceleration is:
$$\text{Deceleration} = 0.445\text{ m s}^{-2} \text{ (to 3 s.f.)}$$

hints: At constant speed up the hill, acceleration is zero, so the driving force balances resistance and the downslope weight component.
Calculate the sum of opposing forces and divide 25000 by this sum to find $v$.
walkthrough:
Apply the condition for constant speed up an incline: acceleration is zero, so the driving force must equal the total opposing forces along the slope:
$$F_D = F_{\text{res}} + mg\sin 4^\circ$$

Compute the sum of opposing forces on the right side:
$$37000\sin 4^\circ \approx 37000 \times 0.0697565 = 2580.99\text{ N}$$
$$1150 + 2580.99 = 3730.99\text{ N}$$

Rearrange to solve for speed $v$:
$$v = \frac{25000}{3730.99} \approx 6.7006\text{ m s}^{-1} = 6.70\text{ m s}^{-1} \text{ (to 3 s.f.)}$$
